A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TailOPT/BiClip research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison; v1's Appendix E is largely consolidated into v2's Appendix D.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic optimization experiments, GLUE and translation evaluations, and non-IID Shakespeare and Philosopher experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds centralized Qwen2.5/SQuAD and ViT/CIFAR100 experiments.

M1.justification: The BiClip operator, TailOPT framework and optimizer combinations are retained. Local-step indexing is corrected in pseudocode, but the intended update procedure is unchanged. Centralized evaluation applies the existing BiClip optimizer.

E1.justification: Section 6.4 adds SQuAD question answering and CIFAR100 image classification, substantially broadening task and domain coverage. Existing synthetic, GLUE, translation and non-IID tasks remain; TED Talks English-French results move to appendix Table 4.

E2.justification: Corresponding synthetic, GLUE, translation and non-IID experiments retain their comparator memberships. The added centralized evaluations reuse the SGD and Adam optimizer families already evaluated in distributed combinations.

E3.justification: Section 6.4 adds centralized fine-tuning with Qwen2.5 and ImageNet-pretrained ViT-base, reporting test accuracy over approximately 20,000 training steps. Retained distributed experiments keep their stated node counts, tuning grids and non-IID designs; no reruns or revised settings are established.

E4.justification: The synthetic noise/tokenization analyses, QNLI clipping/adaptivity comparisons, non-IID evaluations and gradient-distribution analyses are retained. Appendix relocation and figure renumbering do not introduce new ablations or robustness analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies empirical run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Existing synthetic-curve shading and point-score reporting are unchanged; the new centralized curves introduce no additional uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: New Figure 3 reports BiClip tracking Adam on the centralized tasks and outperforming SGD in accuracy and/or convergence speed. Existing GLUE, full translation and non-IID scores are unchanged. Different averages in main Table 2 summarize a reduced language-pair subset, not improved performance.

T1.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C replace RMSProp/Adagrad's O(T^-1/2) claims with O(T^((1-alpha)/(2alpha))) rates and derive a revised Bi2Clip rate of O(T^(-(alpha-1)/(4alpha-2))). Avg-L2Clip's averaging normalization, bound terms and convergence rate also change. These are substantive revisions to guarantees, schedule conditions and derivations.

C1.justification: The central contributions—TailOPT, memory-efficient BiClip and convergence under potentially infinite variance—remain. The abstract modestly broadens the empirical claim from language tasks to varied tasks and models, supported by the added centralized evaluations.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the revised rates as depending on the noise moment and degenerating as alpha approaches 1, replacing the earlier state-of-the-art rate interpretation. Appendix C.1 removes the convex-loss-basin motivation for neural-network fine-tuning. Existing synthetic-generalization caveats and client-drift interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a public-code link and basic centralized-model details, but removes v1's H100/L40S/A40 hardware description and task-specific GLUE epoch counts, including the local-epoch synchronization explanation. Hyperparameter sweep grids and selected values are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting the new models and datasets, trims federated-application and convex-loss-background literature, and revises the convergence-rate comparison with prior work. TailOPT's broader positioning against clipping and adaptive distributed optimizers remains.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact. Wording is refined, background and dataset descriptions are shortened, Appendix E is consolidated into D, and centralized-learning, acknowledgement and impact sections are added. Citation style and affiliations also change.

P2.justification: The main paper is reformatted into a two-column conference layout with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. Figure 1 changes from a horizontal strip to a 2-by-2 arrangement; Table 2 becomes a compact subset with full results in the appendix. A new two-panel Figure 3 is added.

improvement.justification: The added centralized experiments and code link improve empirical breadth and access information, but v2 removes useful training and hardware details. Its revised Theorem 1 also requires omega-zeta-1/2 > 0, while Corollary 1 sets omega = 0 and zeta > 0, creating an internal contradiction. These gains and theoretical/reproducibility drawbacks prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
